summary: FloodSense AI is a foundational deep-learning disaster forecasting platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Currently in its initial basic phase and designed to scale with vastly more data inputs in the future, the live web application uses NASA GPM IMERG telemetry and a custom PyTorch neural network to predict and map regional flood risks across India up to a full 52-week horizon—transforming complex satellite data into interactive risk heatmaps and actionable emergency schedules.
details:
FloodSense AI is an advanced, deep-learning-powered disaster forecasting platform designed to predict, simulate, and map regional flood risks across India up to a 52-week horizon. The platform operates by processing high-resolution NASA Earth telemetry—including GPM IMERG precipitation data, rootzone soil moisture, evapotranspiration, GRACE water storage anomalies, and topographical features (elevation and flow accumulation).

At its core is a custom PyTorch deep neural network, a multi-layer perceptron featuring batch normalization, dropout regularization, and cross-entropy loss classification. The model evaluates multi-variable feature vectors to classify flood severity into clear operational tiers (Safe, Moderate Watch, and Severe Emergency). The live application features an interactive 1-year forecasting simulator, all-India Plotly spatial risk heatmaps, regional basin filters (Assam, Western Ghats, Gujarat, Gangetic Plain), and automated chronological severe flood emergency schedules.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • Proactive Rather Than Reactive: Traditional warning systems react to active downpours. FloodSense AI provides a full 52-week predictive horizon, allowing disaster management authorities and local communities to prepare months in advance.
  • Targeted Resource Allocation: By pinpointing specific vulnerable river basins and chronological event windows, agencies can preposition emergency supplies, reinforce riverbanks, and evacuate high-risk zones efficiently.
  • Democratized Access: Deployed live on the cloud, the platform bridges the gap between complex NASA satellite telemetry and practical, actionable disaster intelligence for local administrators and researchers.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies Used:

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Deep Learning & Data Science: PyTorch, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn
  • Web Application & UI Framework: Streamlit (Deployed live on Streamlit Community Cloud)
  • Spatial Mapping & Visualization: Plotly
  • NASA Data Sources: NASA GPM IMERG, soil moisture telemetry, and topographical runoff indices.

Creativity & Innovation: FloodSense AI transforms raw, abstract satellite telemetry into an intuitive, interactive time-machine for climate risk. Instead of static maps, our 52-week simulation engine combined with real-time precipitation multipliers allows users to stress-test future weather scenarios dynamically. Furthermore, the automated event-grouping algorithm translates continuous weekly predictions into structured, monthly chronological emergency schedules.

Future Scope & Scalability: While the current platform serves as a robust foundational proof-of-concept, this is built as a lightweight, scalable baseline. In future iterations, we plan to integrate a much wider array of data sources—including higher-resolution NASA SMAP soil moisture grids, real-time river discharge gauge telemetry, hyper-local topographical elevation mapping, and socio-economic vulnerability indexes—to exponentially sharpen predictive accuracy and expand coverage to global river basins.

Design & Development Factors Considered:

  • Scalability & Performance: Optimized model training and caching and lightweight CPU tensors to ensure lightning-fast cloud execution and seamless user experience.
  • Geographic Accuracy: Rigorous coordinate mapping aligned with India's actual river basins, topographical elevations, and historical monsoon patterns (Assam Brahmaputra basin, Western Ghats, Gujarat/Konkan, and the Gangetic Plain).
  • Reliability: Built with robust fallback error handling and relative file pathing to ensure 100% uptime and reproducibility on cloud infrastructure.
